home.title: Welcome to TimeWise
home.body: This is your command centre. From here you can see your whole workspace at a glance — people, hours, costs and pending actions. Let's walk through each section.

dashboardKpis.title: Workspace overview
dashboardKpis.body: These four cards give you a live snapshot: active employees (the demo has 8), pending approvals waiting for your review, open periods and departments. They update automatically as your team logs hours.

dashboardCost.title: Labor cost trend
dashboardCost.body: This chart shows total labor cost period by period. In the demo you'll see several months of data — hover a point to see the exact figure. Below it, the bar chart breaks cost down by department so you can spot where hours are concentrated.

dashboardActivity.title: Recent activity
dashboardActivity.body: This feed shows the latest actions taken across the workspace in reverse chronological order — reports submitted, hours logged, approvals, department changes and more. Each entry links to the affected resource so you can jump straight to it. It draws from the same data as the full Audit log, which you will see later in the tour.

employees.title: Employees
employees.body: Here you manage every person on your team. Each employee has a name, email, department, role, hire date, weekly contracted hours and an hourly rate. The demo has 8 employees across Engineering, Product and Design.

employeesFilters.title: Search & filter
employeesFilters.body: You can search by name or email and filter by status (Active / Inactive). This is handy once your team grows — just type a name to jump straight to that person.

employeesTable.title: Employee list
employeesTable.body: Each row shows the employee's name, email, department (colour-coded), role, hire date and current status. Click a row to open a quick-view panel, or click the name to go to their full profile where you can see their full history, assign a manager, change department and deactivate them.

departments.title: Departments
departments.body: Departments group your employees for reporting and cost breakdowns. You can create as many as you need — Engineering, Product, Design, Operations, and so on. Each employee belongs to one department at a time.

departmentsTable.title: Department list
departmentsTable.body: Each row shows the department name, its current status (Active / Inactive) and the date it was created. You can deactivate a department at any time — employees assigned to it keep their history but will need to be reassigned if you create new reports.

roles.title: Roles
roles.body: Roles define the job function of an employee and, most importantly, their hourly rate used in cost calculations. A role can be something like «Senior Engineer» or «Junior Designer» — the name is yours to choose.

rolesTable.title: Role list
rolesTable.body: Each row shows the role name, its status and creation date. You can deactivate roles that are no longer in use. When an employee is assigned a new role, their hourly rate updates automatically for any future reports.

periods.title: Periods
periods.body: Periods are the time windows that group hour reports — typically monthly. The demo has three periods: January, February and March. Open any period to see all the reports submitted inside it.

periodsTable.title: Period list
periodsTable.body: Each row shows the period name, start and end date, status (open or closed) and the lock date. Locking a period is a one-way action: it prevents any further hour entries and freezes costs for that month — useful for payroll cut-offs. The «Lock» button appears on rows that are still open.

time.title: Log hours
time.body: This is where employees record their daily hours. Each period gets its own report — simply click the day cell, enter your hours (you can use decimals like 7.5), and save. Once the period is complete you submit the report for manager approval.

timeGrid.title: Hour entry grid
timeGrid.body: Each cell represents one day in the period. Enter hours directly — 0 clears the entry. The total and any overtime are calculated in real time at the bottom of the card. When you're done, hit «Submit» to send it for review.

timePeriodsList.title: Your periods
timePeriodsList.body: All available periods appear here. Click any period to switch to it and review or edit your entries. The active one is highlighted with a primary border. Periods that have already been approved or locked are read-only.

reports.title: Time reports
reports.body: Each employee submits one report per period. A report contains individual hour entries (date, start, end, description). The demo shows reports in different states: Draft, Submitted and Approved.

reportsFilters.title: Search & filter
reportsFilters.body: Filter reports by status — Draft (still being edited), Submitted (waiting for approval), Approved or Rejected. The summary line at the top tells you how many reports are in each state across all periods.

reportsTable.title: Report list
reportsTable.body: Each row shows the report ID, the period it belongs to, the employee (or «Mine» in personal view), its status and the submission date. Click «View» to open the full report: you'll see every logged hour, the total, the cost breakdown by overtime rule, and the full status history.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.body: When an employee submits a report it lands here. As a manager you review the hours and either approve or reject with a reason. The demo has several pending reports ready to act on — look at the badge next to «Pending».

approvalsTabs.title: Pending · Approved · Rejected
approvalsTabs.body: Switch between tabs to see reports in each state. «Pending» shows what needs your attention. «Approved» gives you a history of accepted reports. «Rejected» shows what was sent back for correction — each card shows the employee name, period, total hours logged and the date it was submitted.

approvalsList.title: Approval cards
approvalsList.body: Each card shows the employee, the period, the total hours logged and when the report was submitted. Expand a card to see the daily breakdown before deciding. Hit «Approve» to accept or «Reject» to send it back with a note explaining what needs correcting.

costing.title: Costing
costing.body: Costing turns approved hours into labor costs. It applies your overtime rules (daily and weekly multipliers) to each employee's hourly rate and gives you a full cost breakdown — by period, by department and by employee.

costingKpis.title: Cost summary
costingKpis.body: These four cards show the total cost, regular cost, overtime cost and average hourly rate for the selected period. Use the period selector in the top-right to switch between months.

costingByDept.title: Cost by department
costingByDept.body: The bar chart breaks total cost by department, colored with your department palette. The breakdown list on the right shows each department's share as a percentage — useful for spotting cost concentration.

costingByEmployee.title: Cost by employee
costingByEmployee.body: This table shows cost per employee: their hourly rate, total hours, overtime hours and total cost. You can export this as a CSV for payroll or finance — click «Export CSV» in the header.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.body: The audit log is the complete tamper-evident history of everything that has happened in this workspace — every login, hour entry, approval, department change and more. Only admins can see it.

auditFilters.title: Filtering events
auditFilters.body: You can narrow down events by action name (e.g. "time_report.submitted"), resource type (e.g. "TimeReport"), outcome (Success / Failure) and by actor. The filter is live — results update as you type, without pressing enter.

auditTable.title: Event rows
auditTable.body: Each row shows when it happened, who did it, the action code, the affected resource and whether it succeeded. Click any row to expand it and see the full metadata payload. Admins can also attach notes to any event — useful for flagging incidents or adding investigation context. Clickable resource links let you jump straight to the affected report, period or employee.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body: Settings is where you configure the workspace itself. You have four sections: Organization (name, country, currency), Departments, Cost rules (overtime multipliers) and Members. Let's take a closer look.

settingsTabs.title: Four settings sections
settingsTabs.body: Settings has four tabs: Organization, Departments, Cost rules and Members. Let's step through each one.

settingsOrg.title: Organization
settingsOrg.body: Here you set the workspace identity: public name, legal name, country, default timezone and the currency used across all cost calculations. Changes here affect every report and export in the workspace.

settingsDepts.title: Departments tab
settingsDepts.body: You can also manage departments directly from Settings without leaving this page. Create, rename or deactivate departments here — changes apply immediately to the employee directory and cost reports.

settingsCostRules.title: Cost rules
settingsCostRules.body: Cost rules define how overtime is calculated. You set the weekly threshold (hours before weekly OT kicks in), the daily threshold (hours before daily OT kicks in) and the multipliers for each (e.g. ×1.5 for weekly OT, ×2 for daily OT). All costing and reports use these figures.

settingsMembers.title: Members — who can log in
settingsMembers.body: The Members tab controls who has access to this workspace and with what role. You can invite a user and link them to an employee profile so their hours are tracked under their account. Roles range from Employee (can only log their own hours) to Owner (full admin access).

finish.title: You're all set! 🎉
finish.body: That's the full tour. Whenever you want to replay it, just click this button — the compass icon in the header. It's always there.
